class: One undifferentiated auto-submit switch: no review-vs-hybrid choice and no daily cap, so eligible applications either all wait or all send
fix: New submit_policy.py over (never instead of) the safety verdict: SUBMIT_MODE review holds everything, hybrid submits eligible applications until AUTO_SUBMIT_DAILY_CAP (default 10, 0 kills), unknown modes wait loudly, and unset mode keeps legacy verified-only behavior so every existing test and run is unchanged. hand_over holds with a plain reason ('Verified auto-submit held: ...') and the policy joins the audit payload. Full-auto (self-queueing) deliberately deferred to scheduled applies.
prevention: Submit modes are policy over a safety verdict that cannot be weakened from here; safety.py itself untouched (no approval needed on this change).
root_cause: AUTO_SUBMIT_VERIFIED_ONLY was binary: on meant every eligible application submitted with no cap and no middle mode; there was no review/hybrid vocabulary and no brake for a bad day.
symptom: The owner could not choose 'queue manually, submit the clean ones automatically' and could not cap daily auto-submits.
why_tests_missed: Auto-submit tests covered the safety verdict only; no test asked which mode or cap governed an eligible decision.
